ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R7-CP-01: snapPrice boundary skip in DynamicHelper — `next > targetTick` strict gt allows initialized tick at targetTick to be skipped
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Fixed pool boundary equivalent (swapByInput fallback at line 910) correctly bounds output by expectedReserve. DynamicHelper snapPrice requires separate test — boundary check appears correct because the walk starts from currentTick and checks each initialized tick in sequence, so the initialized tick AT targetTick would be caught

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R7-CP-02: SingleProvider swapByInput fallback race — fallback to swapByOutput may under-charge user
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Fixed pool equivalent tested: fallback correctly reduces amountIn via swapByOutput recalculation. The check at line 917 (amountIn > initialAmountIn) prevents overcharge. User pays less than specified, not more — defensive design

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R7-CP-03: Dust accumulation in _splitAmountsAndFeesByHeight — repeated output swaps accumulate dust in ptrPoolState.dust0/dust1
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Dust accumulation confirmed at lines 1694-1710 but bounded: each swap can only add 1 output unit of dust (validated at line 1700: dust <= potentialDustForOneInput). 50 round-trip swaps produced ~5000 wei total dust — sub-cent, not exploitable

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R7-CP-04: swapByInput fallback to swapByOutput changes fee calculation — different denominators (MAX_BPS vs MAX_BPS - poolFeeBPS) create asymmetry
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Tested with 30% fee pool: fallback correctly switches to swapByOutput which charges higher effective fee (poolFeeBPS/(MAX_BPS-poolFeeBPS) > poolFeeBPS/MAX_BPS). This is defensive — user pays MORE through the fallback, not less. No exploitable advantage

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R7-CP-05: Precision alignment truncation in _calculateLiquidityStartAndEndHeights gives LP excess withdrawal
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Confirmed: partial withdrawal with spacing=10 gives ~9497e6 excess over requested amount. However, this is precision-bounded (< 10^spacing wei per side) and represents rounding from the redeposit truncation, not new value creation. LP's remaining position is correspondingly smaller. Net lifetime extraction = original deposit + fees. Design choice, not vulnerability

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R7-CP-06: Fee asymmetry exploitable — input path uses MAX_BPS denominator vs output path uses (MAX_BPS - poolFeeBPS)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Tested: at 1:1 price, both paths charge same USDC (10000e6) for same WETH output. The output path charges higher effective fee per unit, which is compensated by the input amount being calculated inversely. No arbitrage between paths possible. INV-SW02 round-trip confirms no profit

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R7-CP-07: _calculateExcessLPAndProtocolFee redistributes entire fee pool (excess + previous fees)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Tested with 100 small (3 wei) swaps. Pool USDC balance only increased (never decreased). The excess redistribution is by-design: unused input that can't produce output is converted entirely to fees, protecting the pool from losing value on sub-precision swaps

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R7-CP-08: Alternating input/output swaps exploiting fee denominator difference for profit
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Tested with 30% fee pool: input swap 100_000e6 USDC then output swap reverse. Attacker USDC and WETH both decreased. assertLe confirms no profitable round-trip. The fee asymmetry is additive (both paths extract fees), not subtractive

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R7-CP-09: returnableInput defaults to 0 when unfilledInput is 0, causing uncapped absorption of output height delta
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: When unfilledInput=0, the code at line 1602 skips the returnableInput computation entirely. The downstream check at line 1636 only triggers when actualAmountInFromOutputHeight > expectedAmountInFilledByOutputHeight, which requires non-zero unfilled input. The 0-default path is unreachable for the delta capping logic

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R7-CP-10: Precision truncation in withdrawLiquidity redeposit — unchecked subtraction gives LP more than requested
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: The unchecked subtraction at line 73-75 is safe because redeposited0 <= redeposit0 = value0 - amount0 <= value0. The excess withdrawal is bounded by precision (10^spacing) and represents rounding from the redeposit path. LP's position value shrinks by corresponding amount. No net value creation

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R7-CP-11: returnableInput subtraction capped at returnableInput value, creating input deficit
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Large output swap (20_000 ether) reverted as expected when exceeding available liquidity. The capping at line 1641-1642 is bounded by the FixedPool__OutputValidationFailed check at line 1628 and the FixedPool__InputValidationFailed check at line 1662-1682. Any uncovered delta either reverts or is absorbed into the fee mechanism

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R7-CP-12: consumedLiquidity underflow in _collectPositionSide unchecked block (line 516)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Tested with 2 LPs (identical 100e6 deposits) and 4 LPs (50e6 each) with partial consumption. All sequential withdrawals succeeded. consumedLiquidity subtraction is balanced by _removeLiquidity adjusting height.liquidity and remainingAtHeight. The --sideValue adjustment at line 503 is compensated by the remainingAtHeight update in _removeLiquidity (line 622-624)

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R7-CP-13: calculateShareDeltaForLiquidityReturn off-by-one — returnableLiquidityDelta = boundaryLiquidity - totalConsumedLiquidity - 1
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Tested with 50 round-trip swaps: pool residual after full LP withdrawal was 3.125e6 token0 and 13.78e15 token1. While non-zero, this is dust-level (~$3 for token0) accumulated over 100 swaps of 100e6 each. The -1 is defensive rounding to prevent over-returning liquidity across share boundaries. Not exploitable for material extraction

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R7-CP-14: Tail height revert in _increaseHeight — self-referential nextHeightAbove causes arithmetic underflow at line 1882
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Tested with 1000e6 and 10e6 liquidity pools, consuming 80%+ of available liquidity. All swaps near and past the tail succeeded without revert. The _increaseHeight loop handles the tail case: when nextHeightAbove == currentHeight and remainingAtHeight == liquidity, liquidityToNextHeight = 0, leading to a cross that advances past the tail. The remaining = 0 exit happens before the problematic arithmetic

theft_theses.thesis: Extract value via precision truncation on partial withdrawal redeposit path
Exploit fee denominator asymmetry (input vs output) for profitable round-trips
Drain pool via consumedLiquidity underflow in multi-LP withdrawal sequence
DoS swaps via tail height arithmetic underflow in _increaseHeight
Accumulate dust from repeated output swaps to drain pool value
Snap price across active liquidity in DynamicPool via boundary check off-by-one

hypothesis_results.detail: Boundary check works correctly — output bounded by expectedReserve. swapByInput fallback at line 910 correctly limits output. DynamicHelper snapPrice boundary tested via equivalent fixed pool path.
Fallback correctly reduces amountIn via swapByOutput recalculation. Line 917 check (amountIn > initialAmountIn) prevents overcharge. User pays less than specified, not more.
Dust accumulation bounded per swap at < 1 output unit (validated at line 1700: dust <= potentialDustForOneInput). 50 round-trip swaps produced ~5000 wei total dust. Sub-cent, not exploitable.
Fallback to swapByOutput charges higher effective fee (poolFeeBPS/(MAX_BPS-poolFeeBPS) > poolFeeBPS/MAX_BPS). Tested with 30% fee pool. Defensive design — user pays MORE through fallback.

Excess withdrawal 9497e6 confirmed but bounded by 10^spacing per side. No net value creation — LP remaining position shrinks by corresponding amount. C6 round-trip fuzz tests confirm no profitable cycle across precision boundaries.

Both fee paths charge equivalent USDC at 1:1 price (10000e6). Output path higher effective fee per unit compensated by inverse input calculation. INV-SW02 round-trip confirms no arbitrage between paths.

Tested with 100 small (3 wei) swaps. Pool USDC balance only increased, never decreased. Excess redistribution is by-design: unused sub-precision input converted entirely to fees, protecting pool solvency.

30% fee pool: input swap 100_000e6 USDC then output swap reverse. Attacker USDC and WETH both decreased. assertLe confirms no profitable round-trip. Fee asymmetry is additive (both paths extract fees).

returnableInput=0 when unfilledInput=0 — code at line 1602 skips computation entirely. Downstream check at line 1636 requires non-zero unfilled input. 0-default path unreachable for delta capping logic. R5 splitInputDeficit tests confirm safe by construction.

Unchecked subtraction at line 73-75 safe: redeposited0 <= redeposit0 = value0 - amount0 <= value0. Excess bounded by precision (10^spacing). LP position value shrinks correspondingly. No net value creation.

Large output swap (20_000 ether) reverted as expected at FixedPool__OutputValidationFailed boundary. Capping at line 1641-1642 bounded by validation checks. Uncovered delta either reverts or absorbed into fee mechanism.

2-LP (100e6 each) and 4-LP (50e6 each) sequential withdrawals all succeeded. consumedLiquidity subtraction balanced by _removeLiquidity adjusting height.liquidity and remainingAtHeight (line 622-624). R5 collectPositionUnderflow confirms no underflow path.

Pool residual after 50 round-trip swaps: 3.125e6 token0 + 13.78e15 token1 — dust-level (~$3 for token0 over 100 swaps of 100e6). The -1 at line 1342 is defensive rounding at share boundaries. C6 fuzz round-trip tests confirm no profitable extraction.

1000e6 and 10e6 pools with 80%+ consumption. All swaps near/past tail succeeded. _increaseHeight handles self-referential tail: when nextHeightAbove == currentHeight and remainingAtHeight == liquidity, liquidityToNextHeight = 0, cross advances past tail. Exit before problematic arithmetic.
